import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date column to datetime
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Extract the day of the week for analysis
coffee_sales['day_of_week'] = coffee_sales['date'].dt.day_name()

# Calculate total sales per day of the week
sales_per_day = coffee_sales.groupby('day_of_week')['total'].sum().reindex(
    ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday'])

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x=sales_per_day.index, y=sales_per_day.values, palette='viridis')

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Day of the Week', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Day of the Week', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-labels for better readability
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date column to datetime
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Extract the day of the week for analysis
coffee_sales['day_of_week'] = coffee_sales['date'].dt.day_name()

# Calculate total sales per day of the week
sales_per_day = coffee_sales.groupby('day_of_week')['total'].sum().reindex(
    ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday'])

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x=sales_per_day.index, y=sales_per_day.values, palette='viridis')

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Day of the Week', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Day of the Week', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-labels for better readability
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
